are effortless means for the increase of Your grace.
The sages have declared that these [teachings] bestow liberation quickly; you should apply yourself to them.
O Infinite One! He who has sought refuge in You with his whole being, having abandoned all worldly duties—he is neither a debtor nor a servant even to the celestial sages and the ancestors.
For as long as he remains fixed in his heart upon You, You surely dispel every single transgression that may have arisen within him.
O Lord of the City of Wind! Bestow upon me devotion that may restrain the torments arising from my sins.

Out of compassion for you, I shall indeed abandon affection for my kinsmen; having surrendered my soul to you and renounced everything, I shall wander through the entire world, perceiving it as a mere play of illusion.
Since the perception of diversity arises from delusion, when there is true understanding of virtue and vice, there is indeed no injunction or prohibition.
Or how could there be any prohibition against those two for you, whose mind is fixed upon them and whose intellect is free from all partiality?

There are infinite living beings whose minds are constantly fixed merely upon hunger and thirst; among them, because of their possession of discernment (*vijñāna*), the human being here is superior, yet even such a birth is difficult to obtain.
Furthermore, even among those, one may become either a friend or an enemy to oneself—he who has fixed his mind upon You.
For he who remembers the means for the cessation of suffering is a true friend; anyone other than him is an enemy of one's own self.

O Infinite One! When Your compassion is active, who indeed is not a teacher even in worldly conduct? For even though the earth is trodden upon by all, it does not waver; from that, I shall learn true patience.
O Lord! May I acquire non-attachment toward various sense objects, just as the wind remains unattached even when passing through them.
And may my self’s pervasiveness and its stainlessness shine forth by the grace of the Guru of the Sky.
May I be transparent, purifying, and sweet like water; like fire, may I not grasp at faults even when consuming all things, and may I perceive myself as such within all beings.
May I know that, just as the moon has neither gain nor loss of its body apart from its phases, so too there is no growth or decay for the Self.
And by your grace, may I attain unity within my own body, like the sun reflected separately in various vessels of water.
Out of affection, may I not become like the dead pigeon who was cherished by his sons;
may I endure hunger even as a lion does when he eats what he has obtained; may I be unfathomable like the ocean;
may I not fall among women and the like like a moth into a flame; and may I partake of the essence like a bee.
May I indeed become so, O Lord, but let me not enter into it through the power of hoarding wealth.

May I not be bound by a young woman like an elephant by a female in heat; may I not fail to acquire a flood of wealth, for another will seize it from me like a honey-thief from a deer; may I not be captivated by vulgar songs like a wild beast;
and may I not become overly attached to food, like a fish at a hook, but remain free from such desires like Piṅgalā.
O Lord! Because of the necessity of supporting my dependents, may I sleep like a curlew with its prey, so that I am not slain by others.
O Lord, having abandoned pride, may I live happily like a very young child; remaining alone like the solitary bracelet of a maiden, free from mutual noise;
with my mind fixed on You, may I not perceive another, like an arrow-maker who does not notice the soundless approach of a king.
I dwell in houses built by others, like a snake in the burrows of a mouse.
"I realize from the spider that the world you have created resides only within you, and that you alone dissolve it;

from the weaver, may I firmly learn to fashion my own nature through meditation upon you. And may I become one whose very self is excrement and ashes—that excellent teacher who bestows discernment and dispassion."
But when it is contemplated by me, it brings forth many afflictions, especially since this [body] is tormented by manifold diseases.

Hī hī! O Lord of the City of Wind (Kubera)! Abandon this delusion regarding my body! For the sake of that [body], people are bound by affection to their homes, their minds, their wives, and so forth, and thus they forget Your feet.
Such a person is now, and hereafter, no better than a dog or a fire—[one whose] eyes and ears [are only for these things].
The skin, tongue, and other senses drag one away helplessly from here and there; therefore, no one [should turn away] from the lotus of your feet.

O Lotus-eyed One! If the delusion regarding the body is now difficult to ward off, then, having eradicated all diseases without exception, make your devotion to Your lotus-feet most firm. Indeed, at the end of various births, you have attained this Brahmin body which bestows liberation.
Alas, O Māruteśa! Do not cast me into this base flavor of sense-objects; protect me!

But diversity, grossness, thinness, and so forth, are superimposed upon you through association with the qualities of the vital force, just as largeness, smallness, brilliance, or dullness are [superimposed] upon different pieces of wood by fire.

When the dense forest of the delusion of karma, its latent impressions, and the resulting bodies and worlds is being consumed by the fire of clear awakening— kindled by the piercing [of the central channel] through the upper fire-drill of the disciple, which meets the lower fire-drill known as the Teacher— [the yogi attains liberation].
When the fuel to be burned has vanished and the fire of knowledge has subsided, that state is indeed identical with You.
Thus, indeed, there is no other means for the destruction of all afflictions than attaining You;

neither agriculture, nor medicine, nor the six political expedients, nor the six types of ritual action, nor even the paths of the Vedas—though they may be rendered ineffective by defects—are capable of providing results that are both certain and eternal. Even those who have attained the fruits of those paths have not reached such certainty or permanence.
But the intoxicated ones, forgetting you, fall into ruin and undergo endless despair.

Where indeed is there another world free from fear compared to Your world, since even at the end of two *parārdhas*, O Lotus-navelled One, the Lotus-born Brahmā dwells not happily even in the heavenly realm out of fear of You?
If this is so, what need is there to speak of the denizens of hell, who are submerged in the thick darkness earned by their own unrighteousness?
Therefore, O Giver of Boons, O Friend of the Wretched, O Ocean of the Flood of Compassion, sever that bond for me!
O All-pervading Lord! In reality, bondage and liberation do not belong to me, for they are merely Yours;
yet through the forms of Māyā and Vidya, You have fashioned these two, which are like dreaming and waking.
When the bound soul has attained liberation while still living, there remains only that much difference, and even then, You alone remain.
Abiding in the tree of the body, he enjoys the flavorful fruits of the sense-objects; no other is free from suffering.

What is the use of words such as "liberation while living" (jīvanmukti) for one whose intellect is impure? That state remains far, far away; and for a mind that is not purified, there is no means of purification other than devotion.
Therefore, O Viṣṇu, may You grant me the burden of devotion, having offered all my actions unto You.
By which I may quickly become one whose self is awakened by you through the merging of your words with my own.
Even here, some whose minds are devoted to the Brahman of Sound do not know you; alas, their efforts are in vain, for they have carried this earth for a long time without fruit—
she from whom arise your divine incarnations with playful descents that delight the entire world and remove all impurity.
I would not utter that speech which describes Your form as being dense with consciousness.

O Enemy of Caidya! I do not understand at all who you are, how much you are, or what you are like; yet, with my heart fixed on no other, I devote myself solely to your worship, performing the sight, touch, and other services toward your emblems and the assemblies of those dear to your feet.
Out of fear of me, even your respect for worshiping, bowing, praising, and proclaiming my virtues and deeds has ceased.

O Lord! Whatever may be obtained, all that is offered unto You; I am Your servant, and let my constant labor consist of sweeping Your abode and other such tasks, performed with a mind free from artifice. I worship You, whose four arms shine forth as the Sun, Fire, the Brahmin, and the Self.
May my yoga of devotion, characterized by being moistened with love for you, flow forth perpetually.
That singular state of yours, difficult to attain through charity, the Himalayas, vows, observances, austerity, Sāṅkhya, or Yoga—
O Gopīs, it is said that the most virtuous among you have attained that very state of intense bliss solely through association with you;
yet, despite there being many other devotees, you hold them in high regard only for their devotion to you.
Therefore, O Kṛṣṇa, Lord of Vātālaya, strengthen my devotion to you alone and remove my afflictions.

In the beginning, O Source of the Universe, you assumed the form of Hiranyagarbha, consisting of the undivided individual soul; having attained the state of a living being, you abide there, inlaid with the multitude of qualities of Māyā.
Therein, through the increased quality of Sattva, which has attained a state of devotion, the pair of qualities—
Having cut through [the bonds] and abandoned existence, I shall proceed once more unattached—just as you yourself do.

O Lord! Due to the awakening of *sattva*, even when one perceives the defects in the taste of sense objects, activity toward them persists again and again; for when *rajas* is roused in the thick darkness of ignorance, such activity is difficult to restrain.
As long as the mind and the *guṇas* are thus mutually entangled here, it is impossible to obstruct all of them.
But regarding the fourth state, You, in the form of a swan, declared that single-minded devotion to You alone is the refuge.
O Kṛṣṇa! Although there are many higher goals fashioned for practitioners according to their diverse inclinations— along with limited pleasures, peaceful states, and various destinies—
You have indeed declared to Your friend that among all these goals, devotional service alone is the most honored.
Indeed, by what means could the joy of those who indulge in sense objects ever be equal to the bliss born of devotion to you?

For one whose mind is satisfied by devotion to you, who moves happily in this world with all desires fallen away, all hopes shall consist of bliss alone— just as for one dwelling within the depths of water, all things consist of water.
Such a person indeed regards the realm of Indra, the abode of Brahmā, and the heart-pleasing perfections of yoga as nothing more than straw.
Let this remain as it is; he does not even desire the bliss of liberation, being himself free from effort when it has spontaneously arrived.
Your devotee, even when assailed by the pleasures of the senses for the sake of their lack of tranquility, cannot be conquered again by those same weak senses as they are overcome by devotion alone;
just as a fire with seven flames, its rays blazing, consumes a vast mass of wood.
In the same way, the flood of devotion to you burns away evil; where then is the power of the intoxicated senses?

Aside from the moistening of the heart, the bristling of hair upon the body, and tears of joy, how else could the mind be purified? What indeed is the use of extensive austerities or knowledge for one devoid of devotion?
This self of mine is being constantly cleansed by the ointment perfected through the savoring of your verses.
One resorts to the subtle reality with the eye [of wisdom], but not through millions of logical arguments, however well-practiced they may be.

I shall practice meditation, seated with my body composed in equanimity and bliss, my gaze fixed on the tip of my nose; having mastered the pathways of the breath through practices such as inhalation (*pūraka*), I shall turn the lotus of my mind downward.
Having visualized its tip pointing upward, I shall contemplate the sun, the moon, and the fire above it.
I meditate upon you situated there, with limbs as tender as a dark rain-cloud filled with water.

With dark-blue, smooth hair; adorned with blazing makara-shaped earrings; moistened by the radiance of a gentle smile; beautiful with a forest garland and a high necklace encircled by the splendor of the Kaustubha gem;
marked with the Śrīvatsa sign; possessing handsome arms and a soft, radiant belly; and clad in garments of golden luster.
May I meditate upon you, whose thighs are beautiful and smooth, and whose feet are as graceful as lotuses.
O Lord! Holding my mind with ever-increasing curiosity upon all Your limbs, I nevertheless fix it upon that one place—the beautiful lotus-face with its gentle smile.
Therein absorbed, my mind expands within the form of supreme bliss, the non-dual nature of consciousness.
May I not think "another, another" again and again; may I thus become one whose yoga has fully ascended.

O Murāri! When such union with Your meditation exists, may the eight perfections beginning with *aṇimā*, as well as powers such as hearing from afar, descend upon me in a spirit of competitive eagerness. Yet, I do not care for these things which cause delay in attaining You; that alone is what I desire.
O Lord of the City of Wind, protect me from all suffering—you alone who are full of bliss!

For you are indeed Brahman manifest, O You of supreme greatness; among letters you are the syllable *A*, among mantras you are the *Gāyatrī*, among kings you are Manu, and among sages you are both Bhṛgu and Nārada.
Among the Dānavas you are Prahlāda, among cattle you are Surabhi, and among birds you are Vainateya.
O Universal Form! Among the Nāgas you are Ananta, and among the rivers of the gods you are the celestial Ganges in its current.
Among those devoted to Brahman you are Bali; among sacrifices you are the sacrifice of silent recitation (japayajña); among heroes you are Pārtha;
among devotees you are Uddhava; you are the strength of the strong and the abode of the radiant.
There is no limit to the extent of your manifestations; every expanding and supreme reality is indeed you alone.
You are the individual soul (jīva), you are primordial matter (pradhāna); apart from you, there is nothing whatsoever here in this phenomenal world (prapañca).
Those who, with devotion and through dedication to You, perform the duties of their caste and stage of life as ordained by the path of the Vedas,
attain— once inner dispassion has gradually blossomed—
the abandonment [of all else] and realize that which is non-different from all distinct objects, consisting of existence, manifestation, and loveliness.
I am that pure, supreme awakening of yours, which is the root of the universe yet itself rootless, and the "I" that is the ultimate.
Knowledge, action, and devotion—this triad here leads to You. Among these, the qualification for the yoga of knowledge belongs to those who are disenchanted with every object in this world;
the yoga of action, however, is intended for those attached to You, as well as those who are not excessively attached.
Nor are they utterly dispassionate, for their rasa is fixed upon You; indeed, this is the yoga of devotion for them.
By the power of their past merits, those in the mortal world easily obtain either knowledge or devotion to You;

therefore, O Blessed One, whether they dwell in heaven or in hell, they long for birth in that very world alone! Yet, by fate, I have entered this human body, which acts as a boat for crossing the ocean of worldly existence.
Having made the Guru your helmsman, may you cross over, with him acting as a favorable wind.
Those who long for absolute knowledge, seeking the Unmanifest through both scriptural revelation and logic, suffer exceedingly; they attain perfection only at the end of many births.
Indeed, even the yoga of action, though remote from the supreme fruit, is surpassed by this yoga of devotion.
O Mother! May that which is dear to the heart from its very root quickly increase for me, leading to the attainment of You.

The Sage severely rebukes those who exert excessive effort for the sake of mere knowledge; however, for one who hears the reality of Brahman and takes firm refuge in devotion to Your feet, liberation is at the very tip of his hand.
For even in this world, the difficulty of meditating upon You is equal [to that of other paths], owing to the fickleness of the mind.
Through practice, it can be swiftly brought under control by means of your compassion and grace.

O Lord of the World! Though I am weary of the path of ritual action—which is indeed most treacherous—and have developed deep faith in Your teachings and the like, I am nonetheless unable to abandon my desires. Therefore, with my mind firmly fixed upon You, I shall pursue those very desires while perceiving them as defects through a resolute conviction in You.
If you enter my heart, I shall nourish devotion for you alone; all attachments will quickly perish.

A certain brahmin, his mind purified by the exhaustion of wealth acquired through afflictions, was being pushed along by a multitude of people; he spoke thus beforehand: "Truly, neither people, nor time, nor karma, nor the planets are the cause of my suffering; rather, it is my own mind. Therefore, cultivate here a multitude of virtues that act in every way."
Having said this, he departed in peace; O Lord, grant such peace of mind to both you and me!
Just as Indra, having long served Urvaśī with a mind utterly overwhelmed by passion,
became deeply disillusioned and sang that this pleasure of women is merely trivial,
so too did he, having attained devotion to you and becoming fulfilled, move about most happily after shaking off all attachment.
O Lord of the City of Wind! May my ritual action toward you, the crest-jewel of devotees, indeed ward off my diseases.

Indeed, due to the three guṇas, everything in this world— knowledge, faith, the agent, the dwelling place, happiness, action, and various kinds of food— becomes differentiated in form as inferior, middling, or superior;
yet all of this, including the service to Your field and so forth, is nevertheless entirely centered upon You.
They say that by devotedly worshipping that which is established in the absence of qualities (nirguṇa), one may quickly become perfected.
With your mind fixed solely upon you, wandering happily for your sake through all activities,
and resorting to those holy places frequented by your devotees;
with an equanimous mind toward both a thief and a Brahmin, and even toward houses and other possessions, you are being liberated from insults.
May I always worship you among all beings, free from defects such as rivalry and envy.

As long as your nature does not manifest clearly within these [senses], one should thus perform worship; then, in the awakening to non-duality, you will suddenly blossom, and being identical with You, I shall move about.
O Blessed One, let there be no destruction whatsoever of this very dharma of Yours that has been set forth!
Therefore, O All-pervading Lord, grant me with your whole self the delightful path of devotion!
And in order to strengthen this yoga of devotion, O Lord, by good fortune my health and life have been restored; even so, alas, Your feet must be served as medicine, just like milk.
For formerly Mārkaṇḍeya, having heard from the astrologers that his lifespan was but twelve years, cried out in distress.
Having served you for a year, he caused Death himself to flee by means of the multitudes of your soldiers.
That long-lived Mārkaṇḍeya, devoted to you, spent six more manvantaras performing austerities on the banks of the Puṣpabhadrā, delighting in incomparable bliss; meanwhile,
the seventh Indra of the gods sought to delude him with celestial maidens, the Maruts, and the god of love.
But who would be able to conquer your people, who are being scorched by the heat of yoga?
Out of love, you who are named Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by Nara, approached his side;
yet, though praised with joy and tempted with various boons, he did not consent.
With his inner self satisfied by devotion, he instead chose to behold your illusory power once more.
Unacquainted with the suffering that is illusion, he surely seeks even that for the sake of wonder.

When you had swiftly departed, the world— submerged in the seven oceans that were violently tossed by the torrents falling from clouds agitated by the wind— remained submerged for ten million years; yet,
wandering in distress within those waters, he beheld from afar a certain wondrous child lying upon a bed of banyan leaves.
[We worship] you alone, whose limbs are dark-hued, with the toes of your feet resting upon the lotus of your face.
Upon seeing you, the Lord of Sages, his hair standing on end with joy, hastened toward you, desiring to touch you; yet,
entering within by your breath, he beheld the entire multitude of worlds once more, and then,
emerging again through the winds of your breath, he was gazed upon by your sidelong glances.
Desiring to embrace you out of joy, he remained as before in his own hermitage while your body was concealed.
Then, seeking the sight of you, the Destroyer of Cities went before him together with Gaurī;
having bestowed upon him the very powers of being free from old age and death, he himself departed.
Thus, even the Enemy of Smara is pleased by your service alone—for that reason—therefore...
Indeed, it was perfectly evident that you are the sovereign of all, consisting of the threefold form.
In this three-fold Satyaloka, there are the abodes of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, situated one above the other;
and even above those shines the world of Vaikuṇṭha, which is free from the transformations of Māyā.
There, you exist even within the causal waters and among the host of bound souls (paśu), possessing a nature consisting solely of pure sattva.
O Lord of the City of the Wind! You whose self is the non-dual Brahman of Being-Consciousness-Bliss—protect me from all disease.
In whom this [universe] shines forth; from whom this arose; by whom this exists;
who is indeed the one whose form transcends this; by whose light all this is illumined;
who is far, far beyond words, and even beyond the mind; he upon whom the gods, led by Indra, meditate.
O Kṛṣṇa, even the lightning does not know Your true nature, much less others; salutations to You!
He who does not undergo birth, death, action, name, or the manifest qualities and defects of beings in this world, yet follows his own illusory power (māyā) and experiences them himself;
though formless, he manifests in manifold forms, wielding his powers as one whose nature is wondrous.
O Viṣṇu, salutations to You, the abode of absolute liberation, who are completely filled with the supreme flavor!
They say that your form is not an animal, nor a mortal, nor a god or an asura; it is neither female nor male, nor substance, nor action, nor genus, nor even quality, whether existent or non-existent.
Whatever remains when [all these] are negated by hundreds of scriptural citations, that is your form, understood through the function of indirect indication (*lakṣaṇā*).
Salutations to You, who appear as consisting of supreme bliss even when described with great difficulty.

Reflected within Māyā, you create the entire universe— consisting of the gross elements, the senses, and so forth, as well as the divisions of Mahat, Ahaṅkāra, and the subtle elements— which is like a dream or a mental construction;
then, having withdrawn it all once more by your own power of Time, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs.
When profound darkness was arising, you shone forth free from obscurity; homage to you!
O Blessed One! They address You—the sole cause of the universe—who are conceived in every way as the essence of all, as "the Word-Brahman," as "Action," as the "Atom," and as "Time.
Yet that reality which is sung of by the Vedāntas as the Supreme Spirit, the conscious Self—that indeed is You.
O Kṛṣṇa, who by a mere glance brings about the primary nature and its transformations—salutations to You!

That ignorance, which— neither by way of existence nor non-existence, nor indeed by being both existent and non-existent— bears the manifestation of all that is seen, like the perception of a snake in a rope;
that very same ignorance becomes true knowledge (*vidyā*) upon obtaining the face of Compassion through even a fragment of the words of the Śruti.
Salutations to you, who have become the axe that instantly shatters the forest of saṃsāra.
Just as gold is perceived within ornaments, or as clay is perceived within jars, bowls, and the like,
when the ultimate reality is contemplated, that non-dual form of yours shines forth even now—
just as [the rope-nature appears] to a dreamer upon waking, or as the nature of a worn-out rope appears when the illusion of darkness has vanished.
Likewise, O Kṛṣṇa, may [this] clearly blossom upon the attainment of knowledge; salutations to You!
Out of fear of whom the sun rises, the fire burns, and the wind blows;
likewise, out of fear of whom Brahmā and the other gods bring their accustomed offerings at the proper time;
and by whom they were first elevated to their own positions, yet later cast down from them.
Therefore, O Kṛṣṇa, we too offer our salutation to you, the ruler of the universe.

He who contemplates the three worlds as consisting of the three qualities, who is the sole referent of the three syllables, whose form is the unity of the three lords, whose nature is sung by all three Vedas;
he who possesses the three states, who is born in the three ages, and who has traversed the universe through the three steps.
I worship you, who are devoid of differentiation throughout the three periods of time, with these three distinct modes of yoga, day and night.
Victorious is your body— truthful, pure, awakened, eternally liberated, desireless, free from dualities, changeless, and the foundational substratum that manifests the entire multitude of qualities;
it is rootless, stainless, radiant with boundless majesty, and merged within.
The unattached sages [attain] the dense radiance of incomparable, supreme bliss.

May that wheel of yours, which is the very form of Time— difficult to resist, possessing twelve spokes, encircled by sixty joints joined in three hundred [fingers], revolving with a cruel velocity, cutting through the world in an instant as it rushes on— cause distress to others, but not to me, who rely solely upon Your feet.
O Viṣṇu! O ocean of compassion! O Lord of the City of Wind! Protect me from the flood of all diseases!
Who indeed can recount the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu? And who can measure the particles of dust of the earth, by whose three steps alone the three worlds are measured and rejoice in full prosperity?
To that one who sustains all universes, the beloved supreme abode, I shall now proceed.
Where its devotees rejoice, and where there flows a stream of the nectar-essence of the sap of immortality.

He who, with a devoted soul, offers oblations and other materials in the worship of sacrifices and the like to Viṣṇu— the primordial creator of all, the Lord of all prosperity who becomes ever-new at every moment—
and who describes here the great birth of Kṛṣṇa and others, he alone is truly such a person.
Delighted and filled with glory, one should swiftly hasten toward that state which is to be attained at the end.

O praisers, O lords among sages! Just as you perceive Him here, so indeed proclaim clearly the essence of the Veda through the accounts of the divine pastimes assumed by the Lord for the sake of humanity;
and knowing His names to be the bringers of all happiness, chant them aloud.
O Viṣṇu! Through chanting Your glories and other such means, may I indeed attain the realization of Your great reality.
Constantly contemplate in your mind the deeds of Viṣṇu, by which he established the dharmas; those deeds which this servant of Indra performed like a dear friend, bringing about security.
Those perfected in yoga behold his supreme state incessantly; behold it now in its perfect manifestation.
O best of Brahmins, that which is made manifest by those who are vigilant and have offered many hymns of praise;

O Lord Viṣṇu! Neither one already born nor even one currently being born has ever reached the limit of your majesty; therefore, though I am wise, I praise your name repeatedly for the sake of spiritual perfections.
I extol you with various words of praise for the sake of these three worlds.
There, in the world of Vaikuṇṭha, which shines brilliantly above, he has constructed his dwelling.
O All-pervading Lord! At the beginning of creation, the waters produced from the primordial source first held you within their womb;
there, O Hari who reclines upon the waters, all living beings were united with you alone and attained oneness.
Into the navel of that unborn Lord, a single lotus was indeed placed.
That which they call the world-diagram, having the golden mountain as its pericarp and the form of the universe;
Viṣṇu created this world as his own abode; you do not know that there exists within you another form of Viṣṇu. Your minds are shrouded by illusion like mist, and you are deluded by names and forms.
Satisfied with the joy of life alone, go forth devoted to sacrifice; alas, do not desire Mukunda!
O Supreme Person! Having filled the entire universe with thousands of heads, eyes, and feet, you remain even beyond it; yet you shine within the limited space of the heart.
You are all that has been and all that is to be, as well as the body, the senses, and so forth.
For, being possessed by it, you alone experience the nectar-like essence of bliss because it has arisen within you.

Although You assume the form of the three worlds, You nevertheless abide as the essence of infinite, pure gnosis that has emerged from them; such is Your very greatness—what more need be said? Only a small portion of You is perceived as the entirety of the universe, appearing as if it were but a mere third part.
Above that, you shine as the essence of abundant and intense bliss; homage be to you!
Your true nature is unmanifest and most difficult to attain, yet it is pure, singular existence;
and this very same nature is also clearly manifest, like the waves of an ocean of the nectar of immortality.
Therefore, here, let the mind captivate itself through the very essence of your qualities, which are supreme, desired, and enchanting.
I take refuge in Your form, O Lord of the City of Wind! Protect me from disease, O Kṛṣṇa!
First, I behold a brilliance, enchanting with a dense succession of digits; thereafter, bathed in nectar, I see within its interior a divine youthful form,
lovely at the onset of adolescence, my limbs bristling with horripilation from tasting the essence of supreme bliss.
It was celebrated by Nārada and others, as well as by circles of beautiful women who were the personified Upaniṣads.

I behold your thick mass of hair, dark blue in luster, with curled ends, exceedingly pure and bound with graceful art; it is made beautiful by a crest-jewel of gems, encircled by clusters of peacock feathers like rising moons, and draped with a garland of *mandāra* flowers.
If one is affectionate, one should also apply a very graceful vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) along the path of the crescent moon on the forehead.

O Lord! Your pair of eyes is heart-stealing, shimmering with the playful movement of eyebrows as restless as the soft waves of an ocean of perfect compassion; it is graced by a row of dark and glossy eyelashes, possesses a dense luster, has the form of broad, reddish lotus petals, and is endowed with charming pupils.
May you, who cool the world with the playful radiance of compassion, cast your gaze upon me, who am without a protector.
With a high, radiant nose; with the regions of her cheeks shining like a mirror of sapphire, illuminated by a pair of beautiful makara-shaped earrings swinging from her dangling ear-loops;
and with the interior of her bimba-like lower lip shimmering with a deeper crimson glow from the emerging rows of her teeth—
May my face shine forth, cooled by a gentle smile that flows with the essence of joy.

Holding with both arms— adorned with bracelets radiant with jewels and palms like crimson sprouts— the hollow bamboo flute, which was variegated by the contact of fingers whose nails emitted spreading rays of light;
and manifesting a most sweet, blossoming passion within the lotus of his face...
Sprinkle the path of my ears with the nectars of the Word-Brahman, which have cooled the entire world.
His tender neck-region was reddened by the spreading luster of the Kaustubha gem rising upward;
his chest was beautiful with the Śrīvatsa mark and the shimmering expanse of the brilliant jewel-sword;
and he wore a wild garland of various colored flowers and sprouts, swaying to and fro.
I likewise imagine a jeweled necklace hanging from your chest like a dangling bee.

On his limbs, with the five-colored rays of his body, he attracts the world with an exceedingly blooming fragrance; though bearing a slender central vine that supports the vast expanse of the three worlds coiled within it,
he wears yellow garments resembling blazing gold heated upon Indra’s thunderbolt.
I meditate upon you, adorned with a girdle of radiant gems and jingling bells, and with shimmering rays of light.

O fair-limbed one, your two thighs possess a dense and smooth luster that steals the hearts of Lakṣmī; fearing universal agitation, they surely keep their entire bodies perpetually covered by yellow garments.
Before those who bow before them, they act as a casket bestowing the treasury of all desired objects.
I attended upon her shadow, which reached down to her two knees, and her shanks, which were broad at the ankles and beautiful.
[He is] one who speaks of the service at his feet as the highest good, as if with the sweet sounds of anklets;

whose toe-tips act like the tortoise that raised Mount Mandara from the ocean of the deluded minds of those bowing before him; and who, by the moonlight of the cold-rayed moon of his lofty, copper-red, shining nails, [provides relief] for those who have taken refuge.
I offer my salutation to that row of auspicious fingers which destroys the darkness of worldly suffering.
O Lord! Your foot-base is exceedingly sweet to the lords of yogis, the abode of those who have attained liberation, and a wish-fulfilling tree that showers the desires of devotees;
O Kṛṣṇa, lord of the city of Pavana, ocean of compassion, may it dwell eternally in my heart.
Having removed all sufferings without exception, may it bestow the splendor of an abundance of supreme bliss.
O Viśvanātha! If I have spoken here without knowing Your greatness, please forgive me;
may this hymn, consisting of more than a thousand verses, lead to Your grace.
You are worthy of praise in two ways: through the Vedic scriptures and by virtue of Your own birth.
May this [deity], abundant with playful incarnations, bestow here long life, health, and happiness.
